deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. The left half of the page computes two even entire power series P(φ), Q(φ) with P(0)=Q(0)=1. They are defined by a coupled differential system, and their quotient P/Q inverts the elliptic integral ∫ds/√((1−s²)(1−μ²s²)), which Gauss writes in the margin. The right half has three things: (i) Gauss's theta/AGM duplication formulas and their inversion; (ii) addition formulas of second-kind type, R(a+b)=Ra+Rb+C·sa·sb·s(a+b), iterated to three arguments; (iii) the derivation of the differential equation satisfied by s=P/Q. The previous page treats addition of first-kind integrals F via spherical triangles with sinA/sin a=μ, and pendulum-type ODEs. The next page continues the P, Q series to φ^10–φ^12 and computes (Q−P)/(1−μ²).

1. DEFINING SYSTEM (left page).
- Equation: PP''−P'^2+Q^2=0, i.e. (log P)''=−Q²/P².
- Companion (right page): (log Q)''=−μ²P²/Q². On the right page both are written without the minus sign.
- Test case μ=0: Q=1 and P=cos φ.

2. FIRST TRIAL (top left). Gauss tries P=1−φ²/2+aφ⁴ and computes PP''=−1+(12a+1/2)φ² and −P'P'=−φ²+…, so PP''−P'^2=−1+(12a−1/2)φ²+…. Matching with −Q² fixes the φ² coefficient of Q. He then sets that coefficient to −μ²/2 (he writes μμ=A). This gives 12a−1/2=μ², so a=(1+2μ²)/24.

3. COEFFICIENT RECURSION (my explicit version). Write P=1+p1φ²+p2φ⁴+p3φ⁶, Q=1+q1φ²+q2φ⁴+q3φ⁶.
- PP''−P'^2=2p1+(12p2−2p1²)φ²+(30p3−2p1p2)φ⁴+….
- −Q²=−1−2q1φ²−(2q2+q1²)φ⁴.
- Hence p1=−1/2 and 12p2−2p1²=−2q1.
- Symmetrically: q1=−μ²/2 and 12q2−2q1²=−2μ²p1.
- This gives p2=(1+2μ²)/24 and q2=(2μ²+μ⁴)/24.
- At φ⁴: 30p3−2p1p2=−(2q2+q1²). Gauss's scratch lines (−1/24·a−(1+2μ²)(1/24−1/3−μ²/6), +1/12(2μ²+4μ⁴)) are this computation, ending with a=(1+4μ²)(1+2μ²). So p3=−(1+2μ²)(1+4μ²)/720.
- Likewise q3=−(2μ²+μ⁴)(4+μ²)/720.

Final result on the page:
- P=1−φ²/2+(1+2μ²)φ⁴/24−(1+2μ²)(1+4μ²)φ⁶/720+…
- Q=1−μ²φ²/2+(2μ²+μ⁴)φ⁴/24−(2μ²+μ⁴)(4+μ²)φ⁶/720+…
- Note the symmetry Q(φ;μ)=P(μφ;1/μ).

4. ODE FOR s=P/Q (right page, lower part). Gauss eliminates P'', Q'' (lines with ∂∂P∂Q−∂∂Q∂P, P∂P−Q∂Q, and the last line containing (PQ'−QP')² and (Q³Q'−P³P')) to reach ∂φ²=∂s²/((1−PP/QQ)(1−μμPP/QQ)). Equivalently, W:=P'Q−PQ' satisfies W²=(Q²−P²)(Q²−μ²P²).

Proof (mine): Put R=(Q²−P²)(Q²−μ²P²).
- Using the system, W'=[W(QP'+PQ')−(Q⁴−μ²P⁴)]/(PQ).
- R'=2[R(QP'+PQ')−W(Q⁴−μ²P⁴)]/(PQ). This is an identity, checked by comparing the P' and Q' coefficients.
- Hence D=W²−R satisfies D'=2D(log PQ)', so D=C(PQ)².
- D(0)=0, so D≡0.

Consequently s'²=(1−s²)(1−μ²s²) with s(0)=1. So s=P/Q=sn(K−φ)=cd(φ, modulus μ). P and Q are entire 'numerator/denominator' functions of cd, i.e. theta quotients times a common Gaussian factor (Weierstrass Al-type functions).

5. THETA/AGM (top right). Here px means p(x) and pxx means p(x²).
- Duplication: p(x²)=√((p(x)²+q(x)²)/2) and q(x²)=√(p(x)q(x)). With p=θ3, q=θ4 (nome x) these are the theta duplication identities underlying the AGM.
- Inversion: Gauss solves A²+B²=2p², AB=q² to get p(√x)=√((p²+q²)/2)+√((p²−q²)/2) and q(√x)=√((p²+q²)/2)−√((p²−q²)/2). This follows from (A±B)²=2p²±2q², and is correct.

6. ADDITION SCRAPS (right). R(a+b)=Ra+Rb+C·sin a·sin b·sin(a+b). Here 'a+b' is understood as the amplitude-sum given by the first-kind addition, i.e. the third side of the spherical triangle on the previous page. This is Legendre's addition theorem for the second-kind integral, E(φ)+E(ψ)−E(σ)=k²sinφ sinψ sinσ, up to sign and convention. Iterating gives R(a+b+c)=Ra+Rb+Rc+C·sa·sb·s(a+b)+C·s(a+b)·sc·s(a+b+c).
- The algebra scrap (a+b)(ab+ac+bc+c²)−c(ab+ac+bc+c²)=… uses ab+ac+bc+c²=(a+c)(b+c).
- The cBsB−cCsC lines are trigonometric scratch.

7. NON-MATHEMATICAL. '1#=209/12 fl.' and '33 7/16<27' are a currency note.
errors: Right page writes (log P)''=+QQ/PP and (log Q)''=+μμPP/QQ. The left page's PP''−P'P'+QQ=0, and the computed series, require a minus sign: −QQ/PP and −μ²PP/QQ. This is a sign slip or a dropped sign convention.

Top left: from P=1−φ²/2+aφ⁴ one gets PP''−P'^2=−1+(12a−1/2)φ², hence Q=1−(6a−1/4)φ². The written 'Q=1−(6a+½)φφ' is inconsistent unless the reading is wrong. Gauss immediately abandons it for the parametrization q1=−μ²/2, which is correct.

Line '∂∂P∂Q−∂∂Q∂P−… = (Q³Q−P³Pμμ)/(PQ)' is presumably meant as Q³Q'−μ²P³P' (derivative primes and signs dropped). The final line '(PQ'QP'−…)(QQ−PP)(QQ+μμPP)=(PQ'−QP')²(Q³Q'−P³P')' is garbled or incomplete. It is probably intermediate work toward W²=(Q²−P²)(Q²−μ²P²) (it should read QQ−μμPP), and it is not a correct identity as transcribed.
The addition formula R(a+b)=Ra+Rb+C·sa·sb·s(a+b) is only correct if 'a+b' denotes the elliptic amplitude-sum, not the ordinary sum. This is implicit.

results.what: Even entire functions P, Q defined by PP''−P'^2+Q²=0 and QQ''−Q'^2+μ²P²=0, with Taylor coefficients through φ⁶: P=1−φ²/2+(1+2μ²)φ⁴/24−(1+2μ²)(1+4μ²)φ⁶/720, Q=1−μ²φ²/2+(2μ²+μ⁴)φ⁴/24−(2μ²+μ⁴)(4+μ²)φ⁶/720
results.modern_name: Numerator/denominator entire functions of an elliptic function (theta quotients up to a Gaussian factor; Weierstrass Al-type functions) with their differential equations
results.usually_credited_to: Abel/Jacobi (theta representation, 1827–29); Weierstrass (Al functions, power-series and differential-equation treatment, 1840s–1880s)

results.what: s=P/Q satisfies (ds/dφ)²=(1−s²)(1−μ²s²), s(0)=1, so P/Q=cd(φ,μ) inverts ∫ds/√((1−s²)(1−μ²s²))
results.modern_name: Representation of Jacobi elliptic function cd as quotient of entire functions; first integral of the log-derivative system

results.what: p(x²)=√((p²+q²)/2), q(x²)=√(pq), and the inverse formulas for p(√x), q(√x)
results.modern_name: Theta-function duplication / arithmetic-geometric mean relations (θ3(q²)²=(θ3²+θ4²)/2, θ4(q²)²=θ3θ4)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, published in Werke III); Jacobi for theta functions in print

results.what: R(a+b)=Ra+Rb+C·sin a·sin b·sin(a+b) and its three-term iteration
results.modern_name: Addition theorem for the incomplete elliptic integral of the second kind

deep.surprise_reason: It is well documented, in Werke III and X and in Schlesinger's essay, that Gauss represented elliptic (lemniscatic and general) functions as quotients P/Q of entire power series and knew the AGM/theta duplication formulas. This page is a nice concrete instance for general modulus μ. It shows the coupled log-derivative ODE system (log P)''=−Q²/P², (log Q)''=−μ²P²/Q², the series coefficients, and the derivation of the elliptic ODE for P/Q. That anticipates the Weierstrass-style treatment, but it fits Gauss's known Nachlass program rather than overturning attributions.

transcription_corrections: 'Q=1−(6a+½)φφ' at top: the consistent value is 1−(6a−¼)φφ. The image may read differently; the term may be an early slip.
'P=1−½φφ+1/24(1+2μμ)φ⁴−1/720 a' (first version): here a is Gauss's placeholder, later found to be a=(1+4μμ)(1+2μμ).
'p×x', 'q×x' should be read as p(xx)=p(x²), q(xx)=q(x²); 'px' means p(x).
'1−A φφ' / 'μμ=A' line: Gauss sets the φ² coefficient of Q equal to −½μμ; the transcription 'A' is his temporary name for μμ.
'(Q³Q−P³Pμμ)/(PQ)' should be read as (Q³Q'−μ²P³P')/(PQ) or similar, with derivative primes lost.
Right-page equalities '=QQ/PP' and '=PPμμ/QQ' carry an implicit minus sign (cf. PP''−P'P'+QQ=0 on the left).
'(QQ+μμPP)' in the last lines should probably be (QQ−μμPP).
'1#=209/12 fl.' and '33 7/16<27' are a currency note, not mathematics.
